All operating notesOPERATING NOTE / 01

An event alert should take the supervisor to the evidence

Watchpost editorial · 14 November 2026 · 4 min read

AI checks site video for defined events and sends supervisors the relevant clip.

Start with the input the team already has.

Video is a continuous workload. The system checks frames for defined events, groups repeated detections and sends only the relevant time window for a supervisor to review.

For security operators managing warehouses and commercial sites. Watchpost looks for events such as an open service gate or movement in a closed area, then gives the supervisor a timestamped review queue.

Make the review practical.

  1. Agree the authorized cameras, monitoring hours and event types with the site.
  2. Group repeated detections so one event does not create dozens of alerts.
  3. Show a time window and reason that a supervisor can verify.
  4. Keep people identification and automatic emergency decisions outside this concept.

One concrete example.

A site has eight cameras and 12 monitored hours per day: 96 camera-hours to cover.

The proposed system samples the footage and groups one open-gate event into a two-minute review window.

Review the timestamped event evidence before classifying the incident.

Keep the decision with the responsible person.

A supervisor checks the video and records the response. No face identification or automatic emergency dispatch. A supervisor verifies every event and follows the site’s response procedure.

The product’s sample workspace lets you follow that chain: source, finding, review and retained action. The example is prepared for demonstration and does not claim measured customer performance.
